newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's ASE Test applies to issue TDRs.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's ASE Test applies to issue TDRs.

text.p: Taiwan's U.S.-listed ASE Test Ltd said on Thursday it had sought Taiwan regulatory approval to sponsor approximately one million ordinary shares in the Taiwan stock exchange through Taiwan depositary receipts.
The application, if approved, would clear the way for the first listing of Taiwan depositary receipts, though regulations allowing such instruments have been in place since 1992.

ASE Test assistant vice president Jeffrey Chen said the plan did not involve issuance of new equity, but merely the sponsorship in the Taiwan exchange of shares already listed in the U.S. Nasdaq market.
"This will not dilute the value of shares held by our U.S. shareholders," Chen told Reuters by telephone.
"Our aim is to give our Taiwan employees and local Taiwan investors a chance to own a piece of our company," he said.

Of the approximately one million ASE Test shares earmarked for the scheme, about half will be supplied from the holdings of ASE Test's parent company, Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc, and half purchased on the open Nasdaq.
Chen would not comment on whether Nasdaq buyback would have the effect of increasing the value of ASE Test shares.
The listing, which requires approval of the Taiwan Stock Exchange and the Securities and Futures Commission, would be made in October 1997, Chen said.
ASE Test, an integrated-circuit testing firm, was the first Taiwan firm to list shares directly in the Nasdaq National Market.
ASE Test is 82 percent owned by Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, an integrated-circuit packaging firm.
